programme: PHOX2B, NPAS1 and GBX2 carry a sympathoadrenal/paraganglionic differentiation and catecholamine-biosynthesis programme. PHOX2B's target set (DBH, TH, RET, HAND1, HAND2, SLC6A2, GAD1, ISL1) is the canonical chromaffin/paraganglionic-lineage gene set; NPAS1 targets TH, EPO, ARNT and ARNT2, coupling the same catecholaminergic output to the ARNT-dependent pseudohypoxia signalling module; GBX2 (FGF8, WNT1, BMP4, LMO3) sits at the upstream hindbrain/neural-crest patterning step that generates this lineage.
role_in_a: In multiple sclerosis this axis has no established pathogenic role. PHOX2B's only MS record is a modest Open Targets percentile (0.25/4340); NPAS1's is a single report tying it to an MS-risk-associated regulatory (DNase-hypersensitive) site; GBX2 appears only as a proposed cell-therapy substrate — hindbrain-patterned, glial-restricted progenitors generated from GBX2+ cells for remyelination — not as an endogenous driver of disease.
role_in_b: In pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma this is close to the tissue's own defining programme. PHOX2B is the master regulator of sympathoadrenal/chromaffin-cell identity and its targets (RET, TH, DBH, HAND1/HAND2) are among the classic genes implicated in these tumours; NPAS1's coupling to ARNT/ARNT2 places it alongside the pseudohypoxia (HIF-ARNT) axis that defines one of the two major PCC/PGL molecular clusters. PHOX2B also carries a direct Open Targets association with the disease (percentile 0.48 of 449 scored genes), unlike any of the other carrying factors.
shared_axis: The more parsimonious account is not a shared disease mechanism but a shared cell-identity signature: both source tissues (paraganglia/adrenal medulla and CNS) contain neural-crest- or neuron-derived catecholaminergic cell populations, so a sympathoadrenal differentiation programme can surface as network-concordant across cohorts without either disease actually running the same pathogenic process through it.
reasoning: The module is coherent and clearly nameable from PHOX2B/NPAS1/GBX2's target genes, and PHOX2B in particular is textbook sympathoadrenal-lineage biology relevant to PCC/PGL, so this is not incoherent. But nothing retrieved connects the two diseases to each other through this axis — the MS-side evidence is thin and tangential (a regulatory-site association, a cell-therapy application paper), so the cross-disease link rests on my reasoning about shared cell composition rather than on documented fact.
support: PMID 30880587 — GBX2+ hindbrain progenitor-like cells proposed as a remyelination cell therapy for demyelinating disease including MS (therapeutic application, not endogenous pathogenesis); PMID 24092328 — NPAS1 sits near a DNase-hypersensitive regulatory site associated with MS risk (regulatory association, not mechanistic). No PMID in the retrieved material places PHOX2B, NPAS1 or GBX2 in pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma — PHOX2B's only disease-B evidence is an Open Targets percentile score, not a paper.
how_to_falsify: Check chromatin accessibility/expression data from MS lesion tissue or CSF-infiltrating cell populations for co-regulation of the PHOX2B/NPAS1/GBX2 target genes (DBH, TH, RET, HAND1/HAND2, ARNT/ARNT2). If these catecholaminergic/sympathoadrenal genes are not co-expressed as a module in any MS-relevant cell type, the shared-cell-identity account fails and the cross-disease network concordance is better explained by coincidental structure or tissue-composition confounds rather than a real shared programme.
caveats: The adrenal|brain tissue pairing has no established anatomical or clinical link outside rare paraneoplastic contexts, so any shared-axis claim needs independent corroboration rather than face-value acceptance. 260 patient-group comparisons across 6 independent cohort pairs give reasonable breadth for the recurrence counts (88-96/260 for the three carrying factors), but well over half the comparisons did not support them either. Single-view factors (CAMTA1, ATOH1, ATOH7, LHX9, STAT4, HDAC5, etc.) were correctly excluded as one-cohort artefacts, and known tissue-generic regulators of these compartments (REST, SOX2, MEF2C, DLX5, STAT4, NR3C1) were removed before ranking — the absence of a general neural/immune master regulator in this account is by design, not an oversight. FOXO1, BCL6 and NR1H3 have genuine independent MS literature support but were left out of the carrying set: they don't share a mechanism with the PHOX2B/NPAS1/GBX2 axis (FOXO1's only PCC evidence is a propofol pharmacology paper on tumour-cell proliferation, unrelated to sympathoadrenal differentiation).
